question: I am transferring from GO to the TTC under One Fare. Why should I keep using the same payment card rather than tap a different card on the TTC?
generated_answer:
You should use the same payment card for both GO and TTC to ensure that you are not charged a double fare. When using the same card, the system will recognize the transfer and apply the appropriate fare.

If you tap a different card on the TTC, you may be charged a second fare for your TTC ride, even though you have already paid for the GO portion of your trip. To avoid this, make sure you use the same payment card for both GO and TTC when taking advantage of One Fare.

It’s important to note that not all payment cards are compatible with One Fare. Check with your payment card provider to ensure that your card is eligible for One Fare before using it for both GO and TTC. If your card is not compatible, you may need to use a different payment method or purchase a transfer ticket. 

Additionally, if you are using a payment card that supports tap-on, tap-off functionality (such as a Presto card or a contactless credit/debit card), make sure to tap off at the end of your TTC ride to avoid being charged the full TTC fare. 

Remember, the key to using One Fare successfully is to ensure that both your GO and TTC rides are linked to the same payment card and that you follow the correct tap-on and tap-off procedures for each mode of transportation. 

If you have any further questions or concerns, I recommend contacting GO Transit or the TTC directly for more detailed guidance on using One Fare with your specific payment card.
